text: 🇲🇽⚽ "You won't represent me or the mayor. You will represent Mexico. There is no greater pride than having you represent us." — Presidenta Sheinbaum to the four World Cup ticket winners Four young women — from Veracruz, Oaxaca, Iztapalapa, and Gustavo A. Madero — won Sheinbaum's personal World Cup tickets through a nationwide ball control contest judged by Charlyn Corral, referee Katia Itzel García, and journalist Gabriela Fernández de Lara.

🇲🇽⚽ "For centuries they told us there were jobs for men, jobs for women. Sports for men, sports for women. Today those stereotypes are being broken." — Clara Brugada, Mexico City Mayor, mañanera May 29 Brugada announced a Guinness World Record attempt on June 6: "La Gran Ola Mundialista" on Paseo de la Reforma. Mexico City will host the world's largest Fan Fest at the Zócalo for the World Cup opening.

🇲🇽⚽ 1.2 million children. 96,000 teams. 28,000 schools. The largest youth football program Mexico has ever created. — Rommel Pacheco, CONADE Director, mañanera May 29 The Social World Cup finals are at the Olympic Stadium in CU today. 24 teams qualified through municipal, state, and national rounds. 106 young talents scouted for professional clubs and the national team.

🇲🇽⚽ "Every football club in Mexico should have its own academy. The boy or girl in the most remote corner of Mexico should be able to reach the national team." — Presidenta Sheinbaum, mañanera May 29 Sheinbaum called on professional clubs to build grassroots development. The Social World Cup identified talent from 28,000+ schools. A pipeline now channels top prospects to professional teams and the national squad.

🇲🇽⚽ "We want this sport to be something social — not just the business side of football." — Presidenta Sheinbaum, mañanera May 29 Mexico is hosting the World Cup for the third time. Sheinbaum's Social World Cup reached 1.2 million children through school tournaments nationwide. 106 young talents identified for professional club pipelines.

🇲🇽⚽ "Football has no gender, no owner, no borders. It belongs to the people — and to girls and women." "El futbol no tiene sexo, no tiene dueño, no tiene fronteras; es del pueblo, y es de las niñas y de las mujeres." — Clara Brugada, Mexico City Mayor, mañanera May 29 Mexico City rehabilitated 500+ soccer fields ahead of the 2026 World Cup. 18 football festivals planned across the city. The world's largest Fan Fest opens at the Zócalo on inauguration day.

📊🇺🇸 <u>FED'S OWN INFLATION GAUGE CONFIRMS 3.8% — 3-YEAR HIGH, NO RATE CUTS IN SIGHT</u>

The PCE index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure — hit 3.8% annual in April, up from 3.5% in March. Gasoline surged 5.5% in a single month with Brent crude at $118/barrel. New Fed chair Kevin Warsh inherits an economy wrecked by tariffs and the Iran war with no room to cut rates.

Meanwhile Mexico: Banxico already cut to 6.5%, inflation trending down to 4.11%, fuel prices stable through IEPS subsidies, and 24 basic products held at 910 pesos through the PACIC. One country chose war and tariffs. The other chose policy.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US ACCUSES 10 SINALOA OFFICIALS — ZERO INTERPOL RED NOTICES</u>

A New York district court issued arrest warrants against 10 Sinaloa state officials. But as FGR spokesperson Ulises Lara confirmed: "Ninguna de estas personas cuenta con ficha roja de Interpol."

Five have already appeared voluntarily before Mexican authorities. The FGR opened its own investigation immediately. Due process through institutional channels — not extradition theater from a Manhattan courtroom. The US issues warrants from 3,000 miles away. Mexico investigates through its own courts.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>MEXICO CITY LAUNCHES 113 HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIONS FOR THE WORLD CUP</u>

While other host cities roll out surveillance, Mexico City rolled out 113 human rights actions covering gender equality, LGBTIQ+ protections, trafficking prevention, and environmental care.

Jefa Clara Brugada's administration trained 19,000 people to spot and report human trafficking and deployed 50 specialized "World Cup points" across the capital for prevention and intervention. The framework explicitly opposes racism, xenophobia, sexism, and classism — feminist, democratic, and sustainable by design.

🌎🔥 <u>WMO: 86% CHANCE THE PLANET BREAKS ITS HEAT RECORD BY 2030</u>

The World Meteorological Organization just dropped its 2026-2030 forecast based on 13 independent models: 86% probability that global temperatures will surpass the 2024 record of 1.55°C above pre-industrial levels.

The Arctic faces anomalies of 2.8°C — more than 3.5 times the global average. A 64% probability of El Niño intensifying toward 2027 means the Global South takes the first hit while the biggest emitters keep subsidizing fossil fuels and starting wars that spike oil consumption.
